html:
Kalevipoeg is the Estonian national epic, put together by the doctor Friedrich Reinhold Kreutzwald and published from 1857 to 1861.

Kreutzwald took folk songs and legends about the giant hero Kalevipoeg, son of Kalev, and wove them into a long poem in the old folk metre, adding much of his own. Its model was the Finnish Kalevala. The hero fights, builds and finally dies, and the poem ends with the hope that he will one day return and bring his people happiness.

Published by the Learned Estonian Society of Tartu, it gave Estonians, then mostly peasants under German landlords, an epic of their own. With the Song Festival of 1869 it stood at the heart of the national awakening that led to independent Estonia.
sum: Kalevipoeg is the Estonian national epic, put together by the doctor Friedrich Reinhold Kreutzwald and published from 1857 to 1861.
